stem.en: A hydra carries several small outgrowths on its body. What are they?

text.en: Spores that settled on the hydra from the pond water

feedback.en: These outgrowths grow from the hydra's own body. Spores belong to moulds.

text.en: Parts of the hydra that have been torn away

feedback.en: Nothing has been torn. These parts are growing, and they will separate later.

text.en: Young plants growing on the hydra as a host

feedback.en: A hydra is an animal, and these are its own young, not plants.

text.en: Buds, made by repeated cell division at one site

feedback.en: Yes. Each bud enlarges and separates to live on its own.

explanation.en: Repeated cell division at one site makes a bud. The bud enlarges and separates from the parent. A hydra often has many buds at the same time.

hints.en: Where do the outgrowths come from?
